question: At the junction between a right-expanded program and left-expanded data, does a flat list [t1 ... tn] transport application: which nesting reading makes the external iota-lang resource definitions true, and from how many elements is the reading decided?
level: Research-local native reduction over two declared readings of one flat-list notation. It is one explicit realization of the junction, not the general representation map: no decoder, no observer and no general program conjugation is claimed.
assumptions: The external declarations are src/main/resources/iota/lang/ski.iota (167 bytes, sha256 cfc922bb5985402e530c61d4effe46952db51b2580c0b3fce735a64a5e6bd995) and iota.iota (92 bytes, sha256 e31b848b4075e402ffb7816c7eea7288ac127230ee10c55a8f5c7a83d1d7eb39) in the iota-lang checkout at HEAD a1865e6d70d55a0d9457b33570e533463818d7d6; these are recorded pins, not read by this run.
ski.iota declares I = [Iota Iota], K = [Iota Iota Iota Iota], S = [Iota Iota Iota Iota Iota].
iota.iota declares Iota x = x [five Iotas] [four Iotas].
The brackets are declared as a flat list; the two declared readings are left-nested (((t1 t2) t3) ...) and right-nested (t1 (t2 t3 ...)).
Parentheses are ordinary left-associated application, as in the case corpus.
The rules, order, counting and limits are the ones declared for the murphy corpus: j a -> a S K, I a -> a, K a b -> a, S x y z -> x z (y z), leftmost-outermost.
These files are definitions, not executable programs: no reducer for the bracket reading exists in the iota-lang checkout, which is why the reading is declared here.

readings.label: R-I
readings.note: ski.iota declares I = [Iota Iota]; right-nested the list is the Iota encoding of the identity.

readings.label: R-K
readings.note: ski.iota declares K = four Iotas; right-nested that is the encoding of K, which returns its first argument.

readings.label: R-S
readings.form: ((([ι ι ι ι ι] x) y) z)
readings.note: ski.iota declares S = five Iotas; right-nested that is the encoding of S.

readings.label: R-iota-rule
readings.note: iota.iota declares Iota x = x (five Iotas) (four Iotas); the declared Iota rule reaches x S K in one contraction.

readings.label: L-I
readings.note: At two elements the two readings coincide, so the identity declaration does not decide the reading.

readings.label: L-K
readings.note: The control that must bite: left-nested, the four-element list is not the encoding of K.

readings.label: L-S
readings.form: ((([ι ι ι ι ι] x) y) z)
readings.note: The same control at five elements.

acceptance: Every declared holding case must reduce inside the bounds and print exactly its expected normal form, and every declared failing case must print something else, with the observed value retained. A case that does not behave as declared fails the run.
residual: This decides one declared reading of one flat-list notation on four declared forms; it is not the representation map the murphy note names. It does not transport observation, does not define a decoder or an encoder, does not connect the bracket notation to the Adva data language, and makes no claim about general program conjugation or about any left/right duality of programs. Native admission remains NotGranted.
